NAHHAS:v5p19/r28.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r28.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p19/r28.claim: Qatada says the Ark remained as a lesson and reminder until the first generations of this community saw it.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r28.anchor: قال قتادة بقيت السفينة عظة وآية وتذكرة حتى رآها أوائل هذه الأمة

NAHHAS:v5p19/r29.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r29.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p19/r29.claim: The feminine pronoun in وتعيها refers to the reminder.

NAHHAS:v5p19/r30.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r30.speaker: عاصم
NAHHAS:v5p19/r30.claim: A reading attributed to Asim is called erroneous because the verb is from وعى يعي.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r30.anchor: ويروى عن عاصم أنه قرأ ( وتعيها ) وهو لحن لأنه من وعى يعي

NAHHAS:v5p19/r31.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r31.speaker: طلحة
NAHHAS:v5p19/r31.claim: Talha is also reported to have read وتعيها, which Nahhas calls erroneous for the same derivational reason.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r31.anchor: وعن طلحة أنه قرأ ( وتعيها ) وهو لحن لأنه من وعى يعي

NAHHAS:v5p19/r32.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r32.speaker: طلحة
NAHHAS:v5p19/r32.claim: Talha is also reported to have read it with a still عين, dropping the kasra because it is heavy, as in أرني.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r32.anchor: وعن طلحة أنه قرأ ( وتعيها ) بإسكان العين حذف الكسرة لثقلها

NAHHAS:v5p19/r33.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r33.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p19/r33.claim: أذن is grammatically feminine, as shown by its diminutive أذينة.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r33.anchor: ( أذن واعية ) ويقال أذن وهي مؤنثة تصغيرها أذينة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r6.claim: Verses 1–12 cite earlier nations as evidence that rejecting messengers brings certain punishment in this world and the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r6.anchor: The history of various nations is cited as evidence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r4.claim: The pronoun in “to make it a reminder” refers to the whole account of divine reward and punishment, not merely the ark.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r4.anchor: is not merely the ark; it is in fact the whole account of God’s reward and punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r5.claim: The account was meant to teach Noah’s survivors, be transmitted to later generations, and remain in memory; people forgot it and rebelled like Noah’s nation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r5.anchor: make them remember it, learn a lesson from it and to transmit it to their later generations

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r7.claim: The ark is a reminder and admonition of Noah's people, distinguishing those who perished from those who were saved; an alternate view makes the whole event a lesson about ancestral rescue and the drowning of deniers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r7.anchor: أي سفينة نوح عليه السلام، لكم تذكرة بما جرى لقومه الهالكين وقومه الناجين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r8.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r8.claim: Qatāda says the ark's remains were seen by the earliest generations of this community; Ibn Jurayj says its planks were on al-Jūdī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: أدركها أوائل هذه الأمة. وقال ابن جريج: كانت ألواحها على الجودي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r9.claim: An attentive ear is one disposed to understand and preserve admonitions; waʿaytu is used for retaining something in the self, while awʿaytu is for putting something in a container.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r9.anchor: يقال: وعيت لما حفظ في النفس، وأوعيت لما حفظ في غير النفس من الأوعية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r10.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r10.claim: Qatāda says the attentive ear has understood God and benefited from what it hears of the Book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة: الواعية هي التي عقلت عن الله وانتفعت بما سمعت من كتاب الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r11.claim: A prophetic report says the Prophet prayed that ʿAlī's ear would be made attentive; ʿAlī said he thereafter forgot nothing he heard.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r11.anchor: وفي الحديث، أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لعلي: «إني دعوت الله تعالى أن يجعلها أذنك يا علي»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p257/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p257/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p257/r1.claim: A transmitted doubled yāʾ is called erroneous, but may be understood as emphatic articulation rather than true gemination or a pause reading extended into connected speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p257/r1.anchor: قيل: وهو خطأ وينبغي أن يتأول على أنه أريد به شدة بيان الياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p257/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p257/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p257/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the singular indefinite attentive ear signals the scarcity of people who understand God, rebukes the many who do not, and makes one truly attentive person the majority in God's regard; Abū Ḥayyān calls this excessive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p257/r2.anchor: وللدلالة على أن الأذن الواحدة إذا وعت وعقلت عن الله تعالى فهي السواد الأعظم عند الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes the pronoun to refer to the known event, namely believers’ rescue and the disbelievers’ drowning.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج إنه عائد إلى الواقعة التي هي معلومة ، وإن كانت ههنا غير مذكورة

RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the pronoun to refer to the Ark.

RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r3.claim: Rāzī calls al-Farrāʾ’s Ark reading weak.

RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r4.claim: Rāzī prefers the event as antecedent: both pronouns refer to the same thing, and the second pronoun cannot sensibly refer to the Ark.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r4.anchor: لكن الضمير في قوله : { وتعيها } لا يمكن عوده إلى السفينة فكذا الضمير الأول .

RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r5.claim: To retain something in oneself is waʿaytuhu; retaining something outside oneself in a container is awʿaytuhu.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r5.anchor: يقال : لكل شيء حفظته في نفسك وعيته ووعيت العلم ، ووعيت ما قلت

RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r6.claim: The cited line uses awʿayt to mean storing provisions in a container.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r6.anchor: والشر أخبث ما أوعيت من زاد

RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r7.claim: Rescue in the Ark and the drowning of others remind people of the Creator’s power, effective will, wisdom, mercy, and overwhelming force.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r7.anchor: واعلم أن وجه التذكير في هذا أن نجاة قوم من الغرق بالسفينة وتغريق من سواهم يدل على قدرة مدبر العالم ونفاذ مشيئته

RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r8.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r8.claim: At the verse’s revelation, the Prophet prayed that Ali’s ear would be the attentive one; Ali said afterward that he never forgot anything.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r8.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند نزول هذه الآية : ( سألت الله أن يجعلها أذنك يا علي ، قال علي : فما نسيت شيئا بعد ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r9.claim: The singular indefinite ear signals that attentive hearers are few, rebukes that scarcity, and says one ear that understands God counts as the great majority to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r9.anchor: وللدلالة على أن الأذن الواحدة إذا وعت وعقلت عن الله فهي السواد الأعظم عند الله

RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r10.speaker: ابن كثير
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r10.claim: The common reading has kasra on the ʿayn; Ibn Kathīr is reported with it quiescent, by analogy with faḫidh, kabid, and katif; 24:52 has a comparable quiescent reading.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94#2/r10.anchor: قراءة العامة : { وتعيها } بكسر العين ، وروى عن ابن كثير { وتعيها } ساكنة العين

RAZI-FULL:v30p95/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p95/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p95/r1.claim: After the three earlier narratives establish the Creator’s power and wisdom, power proves resurrection possible and wisdom proves that it will occur; the discourse then turns to resurrection’s stages.
RAZI-FULL:v30p95/r1.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما حكى هذه القصص الثلاث ونبه بها عن ثبوت القدرة والحكمة للصانع فحينئذ ثبت بثبوت القدرة إمكان القيامة

STUDYQURAN:69:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r3.claim: The reminder may refer to the ship mentioned in verse 11.
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r3.anchor: The it in make it a reminder in v. 12 can be taken as a reference to the ship in v. 11

STUDYQURAN:69:11/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r4.claim: Alternatively, the reminder may refer to the Resurrection and Judgment described in this sūrah.
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r4.anchor: or to the events of the Day of Resurrection and Judgment that this sūrah describes

STUDYQURAN:69:11/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r5.claim: The reminder is compared with the reminder in 50:37 for those who have a heart or listen attentively.
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r5.anchor: V. 12 is similar to 50:37: Truly in that is a reminder for whosoever has a heart, or gives ear as witness

STUDYQURAN:69:11/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r6.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r6.claim: In one account, God commanded the Prophet to draw ʿAlī close, teach him so that he understood, and guaranteed that understanding; then the verse was revealed.
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r6.anchor: According to one account, the Prophet said to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, “God has commanded me to draw you closer

STUDYQURAN:69:11/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r7.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r7.claim: In the more widespread account, the Prophet asked God to make ʿAlī’s ear one that heeds the reminder.

STUDYQURAN:69:11/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r8.speaker: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r8.claim: ʿAlī said he never heard anything from the Messenger of God without remembering it.
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r8.anchor: and ʿAlī is reported to have said, “I never heard anything from the Messenger of God but that I remembered it”

TAB-FULL:v23p221#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p221#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p221#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says God left Noah’s ark as a sign and lesson, so early Muslims saw it, while later ships became ashes.
TAB-FULL:v23p221#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {لنجعلها لكم تذكرة} [الحاقة: 12] فأبقاها الله تذكرة وعبرة وآية حتى نظر إليها أوائل هذه الأمة

TAB-FULL:v23p222/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the ear as one that retains.
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r1.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، {وتعيها أذن واعية} [الحاقة: 12] يقول: حافظة

TAB-FULL:v23p222/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also glosses it as a listening ear, referring to the proclamation.
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r2.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، {وتعيها أذن واعية} [الحاقة: 12] يقول: سامعة، وذلك الإعلان

TAB-FULL:v23p222/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r3.claim: Qatāda says it is an ear that understands what it hears from God and benefits from hearing His Book.
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قوله: {وتعيها أذن واعية} [الحاقة: 12] أذن عقلت عن الله، فانتفعت بما سمعت من كتاب الله

TAB-FULL:v23p222/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the ear heard and retained it.
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r4.anchor: قال: الضحاك يقول في قوله: {وتعيها أذن واعية} [الحاقة: 12] سمعتها أذن ووعت

TAB-FULL:v23p222/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r5.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r5.claim: Makhūl reports that the Prophet asked God to make this Ali’s ear; Ali says he never forgot anything he heard from the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r5.anchor: سمعت مكحولا، يقول: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {وتعيها أذن واعية} [الحاقة: 12] ثم التفت إلى علي

TAB-FULL:v23p222/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r6.speaker: بريدة الأسلمي
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r6.claim: Burayda reports the Prophet told Ali that God commanded him to teach and draw Ali close and that Ali would retain it; the verse then descended.
TAB-FULL:v23p222/r6.anchor: سمعت بريدة، يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول لعلي: «يا علي إن الله أمرني أن أدنيك ولا أقصيك

TAB-FULL:v23p223/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p223/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p223/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says listeners should heed these accounts to avoid disobedience and punishment like earlier peoples; hearts retain the good and evil that ears hear.
TAB-FULL:v23p223/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وتعيها أذن واعية} [الحاقة: 12] قال: واعية يحذرون معاصي الله أن يعذبهم الله عليها

TABATABAI:69:6-12/r18.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r18.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r18.claim: The clause explains why they were carried; the feminine pronoun refers to the act of carrying, considered as an event.

TABATABAI:69:6-12/r19.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r19.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r19.claim: The flood and rescue were made a reminder, instructive example, and admonition.
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r19.anchor: لنجعلها لكم أمرا تتذكرون به وعبرة تعتبرون بها وموعظة تتعظون بها

TABATABAI:69:12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12/r1.claim: The Lord’s general creative guidance equips every kind of creature to move toward its fitting perfection, as expressed in the cited verses.
TABATABAI:69:12/r1.anchor: الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

TABATABAI:69:12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12/r2.claim: Humans share this existential development with material creatures but also develop legislatively through chosen actions that form qualities and states in this life.
TABATABAI:69:12/r2.anchor: والإنسان يشارك سائر الأنواع المادية في أن له استكمالا تكوينيا وسلوكا وجوديا نحو كماله الوجودي

TABATABAI:69:12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12/r3.claim: Those acquired dispositions constitute the human being’s lasting, happy life and the goal of human existence.
TABATABAI:69:12/r3.anchor: وهي غاية وجود الإنسان التي تعيش بها عيشة سعيدة مؤبدة

TABATABAI:69:12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12/r4.claim: This need for chosen moral development motivates religious law through messengers, revealed books, and guidance, completing the proof against people.
TABATABAI:69:12/r4.anchor: وهذا هو السبب الداعي إلى تشريع السنة الدينية بإرسال الرسل وإنزال الكتب والهداية إليها

TABATABAI:69:12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12/r5.claim: Revealed guidance first shows the straight path and leaves humans to choose gratitude or rejection.
TABATABAI:69:12/r5.anchor: هذه هداية بمعنى إراءة الطريق وإعلام الصراط المستقيم الذي لا يسع الإنسان إلا أن يسلكه

TABATABAI:69:12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12/r6.claim: Following the path yields a good, happy life; turning away brings lasting misery, while the proof is established either way.
TABATABAI:69:12/r6.anchor: فإن لزم الصراط وسلكه حي بحياة طيبة سعيدة وإن تركه وأعرض عنه هلك بشقاء دائم وتمت عليه الحجة

TABATABAI:69:12/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12/r7.claim: “A reminder” points to guidance that shows the way: a reminder completes God’s proof but may or may not produce a response.
TABATABAI:69:12/r7.anchor: فإن التذكرة لا تستوجب التذكر ممن ذكر بها بل ربما أثرت وربما تخلفت

TABATABAI:69:12/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12/r8.claim: The aware ear points to guidance that carries a person to the goal; awareness is an instance of being led by divine guidance.
TABATABAI:69:12/r8.anchor: فإن الوعي المذكور من مصاديق الاهتداء بالهداية الربوبية

TABATABAI:69:12/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12/r9.claim: Awareness is not attributed only to God because the passage invites people and promises reward for responding; reward follows awareness as a human act, though it is also attributable to God.
TABATABAI:69:12/r9.anchor: وأما الوعي فإنه وإن كان منسوبا إليه كما أنه منسوب إلى الإنسان لكن السياق سياق الدعوة وبيان الأجر والمثوبة

TABATABAI:69:12/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12/r10.claim: The verse also indicates that external events can affect human actions.
TABATABAI:69:12/r10.anchor: ويظهر من الآية الكريمة أن للحوادث الخارجية تأثيرا في أعمال الإنسان

TABATABAI:69:12#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r1.claim: The author links the reverse influence, human actions shaping external events, to the verse about a town’s faith and piety opening blessings from heaven and earth.
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r1.anchor: أن لأعمال الإنسان تأثيرا في الحوادث الخارجية وقد تقدم بعض الكلام فيه

TABATABAI:69:12#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the reminder is for Muḥammad’s community: though many ships sank and traces vanished, the remains of Noah’s vessel were visible to them on Mount al-Jūdī.
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r2.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج في قوله

TABATABAI:69:12#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r3.claim: The author says Noah’s story in his commentary on Sūrat Hūd already supports this report.
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r3.anchor: وتقدم ما يؤيد ذلك في قصة نوح في تفسير سورة هود

TABATABAI:69:12#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r4.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r4.claim: Makhūl reports that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet asked God to make it ʿAlī’s ear; Makhūl adds that ʿAlī never forgot what he heard from the Prophet.
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r4.anchor: عن مكحول قال لما نزلت { وتعيها أذن واعية } قال رسول الله

TABATABAI:69:12#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r5.speaker: مكحول
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r5.claim: Makhūl says that ʿAlī would say he never forgot anything he heard from the Prophet.
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r5.anchor: قال مكحول فكان علي يقول ما سمعت عن رسول الله شيئا فنسيته

TABATABAI:69:12#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r6.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r6.claim: Burayda reports that the Prophet told ʿAlī God ordered him to draw ʿAlī close, teach him, and enable him to retain knowledge; the verse was then revealed.
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r6.anchor: عن بردة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لعلي

TABATABAI:69:12#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r7.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r7.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet saying that God ordered him to teach ʿAlī to understand; the verse was revealed and the Prophet called ʿAlī the ear that retains his knowledge.
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r7.anchor: عن علي قال قال رسول الله

TABATABAI:69:12#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r8.claim: Al-Burhān cites related reports through Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, al-Kulaynī from him, and Ibn Bābawayh from Jābir from Abū Jaʿfar; it also cites reports ending with ʿAlī through ʿUmar b. ʿAlī, Burayda, and Zur b. Ḥubaysh.
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r8.anchor: في تفسير البرهان عن سعد بن عبد الله بإسناده عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

TABATABAI:69:12#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r9.claim: Al-Ghāyat al-Marām counts sixteen reports on this point from both schools, while al-Burhān says Muḥammad b. al-ʿAbbās recorded thirty from Sunnī and Shīʿī sources.
TABATABAI:69:12#2/r9.anchor: وقد روى في غاية المرام من طرق الفريقين ستة عشر حديثا في ذلك وقال في البرهان إن محمد بن العباس روى فيه ثلاثين حديثا

BURSEVI:v10p103/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103/r8.claim: The rescue and drowning serve as a reminder of the Creator's power, wisdom, overpowering force, and abundant mercy.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r8.anchor: عبرة ودلالة على كمال قدرة الصانع وحكمته وقوة قهره وسعة رحمته

BURSEVI:v10p103/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r9.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p103/r9.claim: Al-Kāshifī says the ship is made a reminder and lesson through the believers' rescue and the unbelievers' destruction; Kashf al-Asrār says it remains a memorial as long as the world exists.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r9.anchor: وقال الكاشفي) : نا كردانيم آن كشتى رابراي شماندى وعبرتي درنجات

BURSEVI:v10p103/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103/r10.claim: The earliest generations of this community are said to have encountered the Ark, whose planks were on Mount al-Jūdī.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r10.anchor: وقد أدرك السفينة أوائل هذه الأمة وكان ألوحها على الجودي

BURSEVI:v10p103/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103/r11.claim: Taʿīhā means to preserve it; waʿy is retaining something within oneself, as in remembering what was said.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r11.anchor: أي تحفظا وبالفارسية ونكاه دارداين ندرا

BURSEVI:v10p103/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r12.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p103/r12.claim: A Prophetic saying describes the good life as belonging to a learned speaker and a listener who comprehends.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r12.anchor: لا خير في العيش إلا العالم ناطق ومستمع واع

BURSEVI:v10p103/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103/r13.claim: Īʿāʾ is preserving something outside oneself in a container, as when goods are placed in a vessel.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r13.anchor: والإيعاء أن تحفظه في غير نفسك من وعاء يقال أوعيت المتاع في الوعاء

BURSEVI:v10p103/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r14.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p103/r14.claim: The Prophet told Asmāʾ, daughter of Abū Bakr, not to hoard or withhold, lest God withhold from her, and to give what she could.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r14.anchor: قال عليه السلام : لا سماء بنت أبي بكر رضي الله عنهما

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r1.claim: The segment quotes an anonymous poet: good endures however long, while evil is the foulest provision one can store up.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r1.anchor: الخير يبقى وإن طال الزمان به

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r2.claim: An aware ear retains what should be remembered and pondered, and does not squander it by failing to act upon it.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r2.anchor: أي أذن من شأنها أن تحفظ ما يجب حفظه بتذكره والتفكر فيه

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r3.claim: Awareness belongs to the heart, but ears convey reports to receptive hearts, so the ear is described with the heart's quality.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r3.anchor: يقال الوعي فعل القلب ولكن الآذان تؤدي الحديث إلى القلوب الواعية

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r4.claim: The singular indefinite ear, instead of plural definite ears, signals scarcity; even one such ear can lead to the rescue and continued life of multitudes.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r4.anchor: والتنكير والتوحيد حيث لم يقل الآذان الواعية للدلالة على قلتها

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r5.claim: One who preserves the story can remind people, encourage saving faith, and warn them away from destructive disbelief, thereby helping ensure communal survival and continuity.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r5.anchor: إن من وعي هذه القصة إنما يعيها ويحفظها لأجل أن يذكرها للناس

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r6.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r6.claim: Al-Kashshāf says that one ear which understands God counts as the great majority in God's sight, even if everyone else fills the space between the horizons.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r6.anchor: قال في الكشاف الأذن الواحدة إذا وعت وعقلت عن الله فهي السواد الأعظم

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r7.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r7.claim: A Prophetic saying calls successful the person whom God grants an aware heart; Bursevī also reports the Prophet asking that this verse become ʿAlī's ear, after which ʿAlī says he forgot nothing.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r7.anchor: عن النبي عليه السلام إنه قال لعلي رضي الله عنه نزول هذه الآية سألت الله أن يجعلها إذنك

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r8.speaker: النقاش
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r8.claim: Al-Naqqāsh gives another version in which the Prophet takes ʿAlī by the ear and says, This is the ear meant.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r8.anchor: وفي رواية أخذ بأذن علي بن أبي طالب وقال هي هذه ذكره النقاش

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r9.claim: Some say the aware ears were named by God in eternity and hear every address from Him.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r9.anchor: قال بعضهم : تلك آذان اسمها الله في الأزل خطابه

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r10.claim: Abū Hurayra explains his many reports by saying the emigrants and helpers were occupied with earning, while he stayed with the Prophet and was content with little; after the Prophet promised that whoever spread his cloak would retain the sermon, Abū Hurayra did so and never forgot the words.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r10.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة إنه قيل على إنك تكثر رواية الحايث وغيرك لا بروى مثلك

BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r11.claim: The account illustrates the effect of eloquent speech; otherwise the Prophet's prayer alone would have sufficed for retention, as in ʿAlī's case.
BURSEVI:v10p103#2/r11.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى تأثير حسن المقال وفائدته وإلا لكان دعاؤه عليه السلام كافيا

TABRISI:69:12/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
TABRISI:69:12/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, in the Qawwas transmission, gives ʿayn in taʿīhā a partly elided vowelless pronunciation between kasra and sukūn; the others read it with kasra.
TABRISI:69:12/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير في رواية القواس { وتعيها } بسكون العين مختلسا وهو بين الكسر والسكون

TABRISI:69:12/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:12/r4.claim: Waʿā means to retain knowledge; awʿaytu means to put goods into a container.
TABRISI:69:12/r4.anchor: يقال وعيت العلم أعيه وعيا وأوعيت المتاع جعلته في الوعاء

TABRISI:69:12/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:12/r5.claim: The cited line says gathering books is useless to someone who does not preserve and retain knowledge.
TABRISI:69:12/r5.anchor: قال: إذا لم تكن حافظا واعيا فجمعك للكتب لا ينفع

TABRISI:69:12/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:12/r18.claim: The drowning of Noah's people and rescue of those aboard is a lesson and reminder of God's blessings, inviting gratitude and reflection on His power and wisdom.
TABRISI:69:12/r18.anchor: لنجعل تلك الفعلة التي فعلناها من إغراق قوم نوح ونجاة من حملناه عبرة لكم وموعظة

TABRISI:69:12/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:69:12/r19.claim: Ibn Abbas says a retaining ear is one that preserves what has come from God.
TABRISI:69:12/r19.anchor: أي وتحفظها أذن حافظة لما جاء من عند الله عن ابن عباس.

TABRISI:69:12#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:69:12#2/r1.claim: Qatada explains it as an ear that hears and then recounts what it heard.
TABRISI:69:12#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: سامعة قايلة لما سمعت عن قتادة

TABRISI:69:12#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:69:12#2/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ says every ear should retain the lesson so it admonishes those who come later.
TABRISI:69:12#2/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء لتحفظها كل أذن فتكون عظة لمن يأتي بعد

TABRISI:69:12#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12#2/r3.speaker: مكحول
TABRISI:69:12#2/r3.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Makḥūl that when the verse was revealed the Prophet prayed, 'O God, make it Ali's ear'; Ali said he never forgot anything he heard from the Prophet.
TABRISI:69:12#2/r3.anchor: وروى الطبري بإسناده عن مكحول أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:69:12#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:69:12#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabari's report from ʿIkrima via Burayda says the Prophet told Ali God commanded him to draw Ali near, teach him, and ensure he retained knowledge; the verse then came down.
TABRISI:69:12#2/r4.anchor: وروي بإسناده عن عكرمة عن بريدة الأسلمي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لعلي

TABRISI:69:12#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12#2/r5.speaker: علي
TABRISI:69:12#2/r5.claim: Ali reports that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet said he had asked God to make Ali the possessing ear.
TABRISI:69:12#2/r5.anchor: سمعت علي بن أبي طالب ع يقول لما نزلت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r3.claim: Al-Farra says the ship itself was made a reminder and admonition for the audience; al-Wahidi rejects this as the better reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: النجعل السفينة لكم تذكرة وعظة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says the drowning of Noah’s people and rescue of the believers with him were made a reminder and lesson.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r4.anchor: والوجه ما قال أبو إسحاق: لنجعل تلك الفعلة من إغراق قوم نوح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r5.claim: An attentive ear preserves and hears what came from God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تحفظها، وتسمعها أذن حافظة لما جاء من عند الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r6.claim: What one preserves within oneself is waʿaytu; what one stores outside oneself is awʿaytu, as with goods put into a container.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r6.anchor: ويقال لكل شيء حفظته في نفسك: قد وعيته، ووعيت العلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r7.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r7.claim: The cited line uses awʿaytu for what one has stored or packed as provisions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r7.anchor: والشر أخبث ما أوعيت من زاد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r8.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r8.claim: Abu ʿImran al-Jawni says it is an ear that understands from God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r9.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r9.claim: Qatada says it is an ear that hears, understands what it hears, and retains it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: أذن سمعت، وعقلت ما سمعت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r10.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r10.claim: Al-Farra says every ear is to retain the story, so it can admonish those who come later.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r11.claim: Abu Ishaq says the hearer should preserve what he hears and act on it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r11.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (معناه: ليحفظ السامع ما يسمع، ويعمل به)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r12.claim: A receptive ear hears, preserves, and accepts what is placed in it by taking heed and acting on the admonition; the meaning applies to the ear’s owner.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r12.anchor: فمعنى واعية: سامعة حافظة قابلة لما يجعل فيها، وذلك بأن تعتبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r13.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r13.claim: The rescue of Noah’s people and drowning of the others show that a directing, powerful agent can do as He wills.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r13.anchor: ووجه التذكير في هذا أن نجاة قوم نوح من الغرق بالسفينة، وتغريق من سواهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r14.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r14.claim: The common reading has kasra on ʿayn.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r15.speaker: ابن كثير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r15.claim: Ibn Kathir’s reported reading leaves ʿayn still, as the imperfect prefix and following letters function as one unit, like fakhidh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r15.anchor: وروي عن ابن كثير: (وتعيها) ساكنة العين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r16.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r16.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r16.claim: The rationale is that the imperfect prefix cannot separate from the verb, so it resembles part of the same word and permits a still vowel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r16.anchor: مع ما بعده بمنزلة (فخذ) فأسكن كما يسكن (كتف)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r17.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r17.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r17.claim: Al-Wahidi compares the vowel-less reading to the reading of yattaqihi with a still qāf.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:12-14/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:12-14/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:12-14/r1.claim: The drowning of Noah’s people and rescue of those with him is made a reminder so later people may heed it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:12-14/r1.anchor: تلك الفعلة التي فعلنا من إغراق قوم نوح وإنجاء من معه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:12-14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:12-14/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:12-14/r2.claim: A receptive ear preserves what it hears.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:12-14/r2.anchor: لتحفظها كل أذن تحفظ ما سمعت

QASHANI:69:9-12/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:9-12/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:9-12/r7.claim: The ark is made a reminder of the holy realm and divine presence, humanity's original home and true abode.
QASHANI:69:9-12/r7.anchor: لعالم القدس وحضرة الحق التي هي مقركم الأصلي ومأواكم الحقيقي

QASHANI:69:9-12/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:9-12/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:9-12/r8.claim: The attentive ear preserves God's primordial address, the covenant and unity, remaining in its original nature rather than retaining worldly falsehood or turning from God.
QASHANI:69:9-12/r8.anchor: تحفظها أذن حافظة لما سمعت من الله في بدء الفطرة باقية على حالها الفطرية غير ناسية لعهده وتوحيده

QASHANI:69:9-12/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:9-12/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:69:9-12/r9.claim: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet said he had asked God to make Ali its attentive ear.
QASHANI:69:9-12/r9.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلي عليه السلام

QASHANI:69:9-12/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:9-12/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:9-12/r10.claim: Qashani says Ali safeguarded these secrets and cites the statement that he was born upon primordial nature and preceded others in faith and migration.
QASHANI:69:9-12/r10.anchor: إذ هو الحافظ لتلك الأسرار كما قال:

ELMALILI:69:10-12/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r8.claim: God made the flood and ark a lasting reminder for survivors and descendants of His power, wisdom, punishment, mercy, faith's benefit, rebellion's harm, and future protection.
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r8.anchor: bir tezkire; unutulmayıp anılacak, önünde ve sonunda Bizim kudretimizi, sun‘u hikmetimizi, kahrımızın şiddetini ve rahmetimizin vüs‘atini

ELMALILI:69:10-12/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r9.claim: The reminder serves as a monument, admonition, and lesson passed from those who witnessed the event to those who did not; it is not knowable by reason alone.
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r9.anchor: bir öğüt, bir ibret muhtırası kılalım da görenler görmeyenlere, duyanlar duymayanlara ansın, haber versin.

ELMALILI:69:10-12/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r10.claim: Attentive ears listen, retain, reflect, act on, and transmit the reminder for later generations to benefit; heedless ears that deny it incur punishment.
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r10.anchor: dinleyip, hıfzedip düşünerek mûcebince amel etsin, zâyi‘etmeyip ilerisi için istifade eylesin

ELMALILI:69:10-12/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r11.claim: The accounts through this point are lesser resurrections serving as reminders; from here the sura begins its detailed treatment of the Great Resurrection, with trumpet passages in 27:87 and 39:68 as parallels.
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r11.anchor: كَذَّبَتْ’den buraya kadar olan beyânât öyle muhtıra kabîlinden olan küçük kıyametler demek olup bundan itibaren Kıyâmet-i Kübrâ olan Hâkka’nın tafsîline şürû‘olunuyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r7.claim: The events are transmitted from generation to generation so all who hear them may take heed, a purpose made explicit in verse 12.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r7.anchor: olayların nesilden nesile aktarılması ve duyan herkesin bundan ibret alması amaçlanmıştır

SULAMI:v2p347#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p347#4/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p347#4/r1.claim: The receptive ears are those that understood God’s secrets; they are emptied of self-witness and of everything besides Him, since the agitation of natural dispositions is a kind of ignorance.
SULAMI:v2p347#4/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي آذان وعت عن الله أسراره . وواعية في معادنها ليس فيها من شاهدها شيء

ITQAN:v2p334#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p334#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p334#3/r2.claim: An attentive ear is one that retains what it hears.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p219/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p219/r1.speaker: بريدة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p219/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet told Ali he was commanded to draw him near, teach him, and ensure he retained the teaching; the verse about a receptive ear was revealed. Al-Suyuti says the report is unsound.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p219/r1.anchor: عن بريده قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلي

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p444/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p444/r1.speaker: بريدة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p444/r1.claim: Buraida reports that the Prophet told Ali God had instructed him to draw Ali close, teach him, and ensure he retained the knowledge; this verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p444/r1.anchor: سمعت بريدة يقول: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لعلي:

AKHFASH:v2p548/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p548/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p548/r1.claim: The verb means to retain or take in: one says an ear retained it, my hearing retained it, and I stored provisions or belongings; an unattributed al-Basīṭ line uses awʿaytu of storing provisions.
AKHFASH:v2p548/r1.anchor: الشر أخبث ما أوعيت من زاد

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p484#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p484#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p484#2/r1.claim: Wa-taʿīhā derives from the expression “the ear retained it.”

MAJAZ:v2p267/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p267/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p267/r6.claim: Taʿīhā derives from waʿā, to retain or understand.

SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r1.claim: The common reading has kasra on ʿayn and a light yāʾ; it is the subjunctive imperfect of وعى coordinated with لنجعلها.
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r1.anchor: قوله: { وتعيها }: العامة على كسر العين وتخفيف الياء، وهو مضارع وعى منصوب عطفا على " لنجعلها "

SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r2.speaker: ابن مصرف وأبو عمرو وقنبل
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r2.claim: Ibn Muṣarrif, Abū ʿAmr via Hārūn, and Qunbul quiesce ʿayn by analogy with رحم and شهد, though the verb is not of that class.
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r2.anchor: وابن مصرف وأبو عمرو في رواية هارون عنه وقنبل بإسكانها تشبيها له ب " رحم " و " شهد "

SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r3.speaker: حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r3.claim: A report from Ḥamza describes concealing the kasra.

SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r4.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r4.claim: The report that ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza geminate the yāʾ is mistaken: the narrator heard its vowel articulated and mistook it for doubling; pause-like gemination is also rejected.
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r4.anchor: وروي عن عاصم وحمزة أيضا تشديد الياء. وهو غلط عليها، وإنما سمعهما الراوي يبينان حركة الياء

SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r5.speaker: حمزة وموسى بن عبد الله العبسي
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r5.claim: Ḥamza and Mūsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAbsī also read with quiescent yāʾ; it may be independent or coordinate with the accusative, and its vowel is suppressed as heavy on a weak letter.
SAMIN-DURR:69:12/r5.anchor: وروي عن حمزة أيضا وموسى بن عبد الله العبسي " وتعيها " بسكون الياء، وفيها وجهان

ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r1.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to this event: the drowning of Noah's people and the rescue of Noah and the believers with him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r1.anchor: معناه لنجعل هذه الفعلة لكم تذكرة، أي إغراق قوم نوح

ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r2.claim: A receptive ear preserves what it hears and acts upon it; Arabic uses waʿaytu for retaining something inwardly but awʿaytu for putting an object into a container.
ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r2.anchor: معناه أذن تحفظ ما سمعت وتعمل به، أي ليحفظ السامع ما سمع ويعمل به

ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r3.claim: Arabic contrasts retaining knowledge or speech with storing belongings in a vessel: one says waʿaytu knowledge, but awʿaytu goods in a container.
ZAJJAJ:v5p215/r3.anchor: تقول لكل شيء حفظته في نفسك: قد وعيته، يقال: قد وعيت العلم

ASAD-NOTES:69:11#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:11#n7/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:11#n7/r1.claim: The reminder points both to evildoers' punishment and to the saving grace bestowed on the righteous.
ASAD-NOTES:69:11#n7/r1.anchor: Alluding to the punishment of evildoers and the saving grace bestowed upon the righteous

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r1.claim: Reports from al-Hilwani and Abu Rabi'a say Qunbul from Ibn Kathir has a still ع; al-Farisi's own reading with Qunbul has kasra on ع and fatḥa on yāʾ, like Hamza and the others.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r1.anchor: روى الحلواني بإسناده عن ابن كثير: وتعيها [الحاقة/ 12] ساكنة العين، وكذلك قال أبو ربيعة عن قنبل

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r2.claim: Al-Farisi read وتعيها with kasra on ع and fatḥa on yāʾ when reciting to Qunbul, like Hamza and the other readers.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r2.anchor: وقرأت أنا على قنبل: وتعيها بكسر العين وفتح الياء مثل حمزة. وكذلك الباقون على وزن تليها

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r3.claim: The still reading treats the prefix and verb as one unit, like فخذ and كتف; he also compares ويتقه and allows a pause-like treatment in connection.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p315#2/r3.anchor: وجه قوله: وتعيها أنه جعل حرف المضارعة مع ما بعد بمنزلة فخذ، فأسكن كما يسكن كتف

QIRAAT-ER:69:12:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:12:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:69:12:4#1/r1.claim: The source identifies tanwīn as the standard reading of tadhkiratan.

QIRAAT-ER:69:12:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:12:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:69:12:7#1/r1.claim: Sukūn on dhāl gives the lighter udhn form; both forms are canonical and carry the same meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:69:12:7#1/r1.anchor: Sukūn on dhāl — lighter form (udhun vs udhn), both canonical; no semantic difference

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p313#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p313#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p313#2/r1.claim: Qatāda defines an attentive ear as one that hears, understands what it hears, and retains it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p313#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أذن واعية ﴾ قال أذن سمعت وعقلت ما سمعت وأوعت

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r1.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to the event: saving the believers and drowning the unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r1.anchor: أي الفعلة التي هي عبارة عن إنجاء المؤمنين وإغراق الكافرين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r2.claim: The event is a lesson and a sign of the Creator’s perfect power and wisdom, overwhelming force, and abundant mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r2.anchor: عبرة ودلالة على كمال قدرة الصانع وحكمته وقوة قهره وسعة رحمته

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r3.claim: Taʿīhā means retain it; waʿy is keeping something within oneself, while īʿāʾ is keeping it in an external receptacle.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r3.anchor: والوعي أن تحفظ الشيء في نفسك والإيعاء أن تحفظه في غير نفسك من وعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r4.claim: A receptive ear retains what should be kept by remembering, spreading, and reflecting on it, and does not neglect acting on it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r4.anchor: من شأنها أن تحفظ ما يجب حفظه بتذكره وإشاعته والتفكر فيه ولا تضيعه بترك العمل به

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r5.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r5.claim: Qatāda says the receptive ear understands God and benefits from what it hears of His Book.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة الواعية هي التي عقلت عن الله تعالى وانتفعت بما سمعت من كتاب الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r6.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r6.claim: The Prophet prayed that ʿAlī’s ear would be made receptive; ʿAlī said he never forgot what he heard and could not forget.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r6.anchor: وفي الخبر أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال لعلي كرم الله تعالى وجهه إني دعوت الله تعالى أن يجعلها أذنك يا علي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r7.claim: Calling the ear a preserver or rememberer is figurative because its owner performs those acts; only hearing is literally ascribed to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r7.anchor: وفي جعل الأذن واعية وكذا جعلها حافظة ومتذكرة ونحو ذلك تجوز والفاعل لذلك إنما هو صاحبها ولا ينسب لها حقيقة إلا السمع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r8.claim: The indefinite “an ear” indicates that such receptive ears are rare.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r9.claim: An alternative makes the pronoun refer to the ark, a reminder when early Muslims encountered its planks on al-Jūdī; Qatāda is cited for the discovery.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r9.anchor: وقيل ضمير نجعلها للجارية وجعلها تذكرة لما أنه على ما قال قتادة أدركها أوائل هذه الأمة أي أدركوا ألواحها على الجودي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj is cited for the claim that early Muslims found the ark’s planks on al-Jūdī.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r10.anchor: كما قال ابن جريج بل قيل إن بعض الناس وجد شيئا من أجزائها بعد الإسلام بكثير

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r11.claim: Some claim pieces of the ark were found much later in the Islamic period, but Al-Ālūsī says their authenticity is unknown.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r11.anchor: بل قيل إن بعض الناس وجد شيئا من أجزائها بعد الإسلام بكثير والله تعالى أعلم بصحته

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r12.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the earlier explanation: the reminder is the rescue and drowning event, not the ark.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r12.anchor: ولا يخفى أن المعول عليه ما قدمناه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r13.speaker: ابن مصرف وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r13.claim: Ibn Miṣraf and Abū ʿAmr in reports from Hārūn and Khārija, with disagreement reported, read with sukūn on the ʿayn by analogy with katif and kabid.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن مصرف وأبو عمرو في رواية هارون وخارجة عنه وقيل بخلاف عنه وتعيها بإسكان العين على التشبيه بكتف وكبد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r14.claim: A further reported reading hides the kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r14.anchor: وقرأ بإخفاء الكسرة وروي عن عاصم أنه قرأ بتشديد الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r15.speaker: عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r15.claim: A reading attributed to ʿĀṣim doubles the yāʾ; al-Baḥr calls it erroneous, while Al-Ālūsī allows emphatic articulation rather than true doubling or assimilation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r15.anchor: وروي عن عاصم أنه قرأ بتشديد الياء قال في البحر قيل هو خطأ وينبغي أن يتأول على أنه أريد به شد بيان الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r16.speaker: حمزة وموسى بن عبد الله العبسي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r16.claim: Ḥamza and Mūsā b. ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAbsī read with sukūn on the yāʾ, apparently as a new clause; another analysis compares it with the reading in 5:89.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r16.anchor: وروي عن حمزة وموسى بن عبد الله العبسي وتعيها بإسكان الياء فاحتمل الإستئناف وهو الظاهر واحتمل أن يكون مثل قراءة من أوسط ما تطعمون أهاليكم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r17.speaker: نافع
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r17.claim: Nāfiʿ reads idhan with sukūn on the dhāl for ease.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p43/r17.anchor: وقرأ نافع إذن بإسكان الذال للتخفيف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r1.claim: The drowning of Noah's people and the rescue of those carried with him were made a reminder for later people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r1.anchor: أي لنجعل تلك الفعلة التي فعلنا من إغراق قوم نوح ونجاة من حملنا معه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r2.claim: Tadhkirah means a lesson and admonition.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r3.speaker: القواس عن ابن كثير وسليم عن حمزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r3.claim: Al-Qawwas from Ibn Kathir and Sulaym from Hamza read the ʿayn with ikhtilās; the other readers use kasra.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r3.anchor: قرأ القواس عن ابن كثير وسليم عن حمزة باختلاس العين، وقرأ الآخرون بكسرها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r4.claim: A wāʿiyah ear is one that preserves what came from God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r4.anchor: أذن واعية} أي: حافظة لما جاء من عند الله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r5.claim: Qatada says it is an ear that hears and understands what it hears.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r5.anchor: قال قتادة: [أذن] (1) سمعت وعقلت ما سمعت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r6.claim: Al-Farraʾ says every ear should preserve the lesson and admonition for people who come later.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209#2/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: لتحفظها كل أذن فتكون عبرة وموعظة لمن يأتي بعد

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r4.claim: The remembered event is the rescue of believers and drowning of unbelievers; it teaches the Maker's power, wisdom, dominance, and mercy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r4.anchor: لنجعل الفعلة وهي إنجاء المؤمنين وإغراق الكافرين

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.claim: To “retain” it is to preserve and remember it within oneself; īʿāʾ is preserving something outside oneself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.anchor: والوعي أن تحفظ الشيء في نفسك والإيعاء أن تحفظه في غيرك

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the word with a quiescent ʿayn, analogizing its form to “katif.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r6.anchor: وعن ابن كثير «تعيها» بسكون العين تشبيها بكتف

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r7.claim: A receptive ear retains what should be remembered, shared, reflected on, and acted upon; the indefinite form highlights how few such people can help save multitudes and perpetuate their descendants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r7.anchor: من شأنها أن تحفظ ما يجب حفظه بتذكره وإشاعته والتفكر فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r8.speaker: نافع
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r8.claim: Nāfiʿ reads “أذن” with a lightened dhāl.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r3.claim: The narrative starts with Thamūd as the nearest destroyed people to Mecca, since nearby warnings are more forceful, and ends with Noah’s people, who covered the earth and were known to all later people.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r3.anchor: بدأ سبحانه وتعالى بثمود الذين هم أقرب المهلكين إلى مكة المشرفة لأن التخويف بالأقرب أقعد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r4.claim: “It” refers to the acts of rescuing believers and preserving Noah's ark as a sign and wonder.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r4.anchor: وكذا السفينة التي حملنا فيها نوحا عليه السلام ومن معه بإبقائها آية من آياته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r5.claim: The story and ark remind people of their first creation and admonish them to recognize God’s power, knowledge, mercy, and might, and to turn to Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r5.anchor: لذكر أول إنشائه والموعظة به لتستدلا بذلك على كمال قدرته تعلى وتمام علمه وعظمة رحمته وقهره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r6.claim: The intended preservation is stable and lasting, as if the story of the ark and preceding events were held in a container.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r6.anchor: ولتحفظ قصة السفينة وغيرها مما تقدم , حفظا ثابتا مستقرا كأنه محوى في وعاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r7.claim: The singular, indefinite “ear” indicates that people who truly benefit from what they hear are very few, while also magnifying the value of such an ear.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r7.anchor: ولما كان المنتفع بما يسمع الحافظ له قليلا جدا , دل على ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r8.claim: A receptive ear preserves divine teachings and secrets for the benefit of God's servants, as Noah and his few companions preserved posterity and blessing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r8.anchor: من شأنها أن تحفظ ما ينبغي حفظه من الأقوال والأفعال الإلهية والأسرار الربانية لنفع عباد الله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r9.claim: “Waʿy” is retaining something in oneself, while “īʿāʾ” is retaining it in a container.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r9.anchor: والوعي : الحفظ في النفس , والإيعاء : الحفظ في الوعاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r10.speaker: الأصبهاني والزمخشري
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r10.claim: Al-Iṣfahānī, al-Zamakhsharī, and others say that one ear attentive to God constitutes the vast majority, while God pays no heed to the rest.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r10.anchor: وما سواها لا يبالي بهم الله بالة - قاله الأصبهاني والزمخشري وغيرهما

DURR-FULL:v8p265/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r15.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r15.claim: Mujāhid explains the aware ear as one that preserves, with a transmitted alternative gloss of “hearing.”
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r15.anchor: وفي قوله: {وتعيها أذن واعية} قال: حافظة وفي لفظ: سامعة

DURR-FULL:v8p266/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r4.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the jāriya as the ship; its survival is a reminder of Noah's people punished for disobeying him, and an aware ear preserves the ship's story.
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r4.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {حملناكم في الجارية} قال: السفينة وفي قوله: {لنجعلها لكم تذكرة} أي تذكرون ماصنع بهم

DURR-FULL:v8p266/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r5.claim: Makhūl reports that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet asked God to make it ʿAlī's ear; Makhūl says ʿAlī then retained everything he heard from the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r5.anchor: عن مكحول قال: لما نزلت {وتعيها أذن واعية} قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: سألت ربي أن يجعلها أذن علي

DURR-FULL:v8p266/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r6.claim: Burayda reports that the Prophet told ʿAlī God had ordered him to draw ʿAlī near, teach him, and ensure he retained knowledge; the verse was then revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r6.anchor: عن بريدة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلي: إن الله أمرني أن أدنيك ولا أقصيك وأن أعلمك

DURR-FULL:v8p266/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r7.claim: In a report from ʿAlī, the Prophet says God ordered him to draw ʿAlī near and teach him so he would retain knowledge, then calls him the ear that holds the Prophet's knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r7.anchor: عن علي قال: قال رسو ل الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يا علي إن الله أمرني أن أدنيك وأعلمك لتعي

DURR-FULL:v8p266/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the surviving ship was a reminder for Muhammad's community: although many ships and traces vanished, they saw its planks on Mount al-Jūdī.
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r8.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {لنجعلها لكم تذكرة} قال: لأمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p267/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p267/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p267/r1.claim: Qatada reads the ark as a lesson and sign God preserved for this community to see, unlike the many other ships that became ruins.
DURR-FULL:v8p267/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {لنجعلها لكم تذكرة} قال: عبرة وآية أبقاها الله حتى نظرت إليها هذه الأمة

DURR-FULL:v8p267/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p267/r2.speaker: ابن عمران
DURR-FULL:v8p267/r2.claim: Ibn عمران glosses the attentive ear as one that understands from God.
DURR-FULL:v8p267/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمران في قوله: {أذن واعية} قال: أذن عقلت عن الله

DURR-FULL:v8p267/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p267/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p267/r3.claim: Qatada says the attentive ear hears, understands what it heard, and retains it.
DURR-FULL:v8p267/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وتعيها أذن واعية} قال سمعت وعقلت ما سمعت وأوعت

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#5/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#5/r1.speaker: مكحول
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#5/r1.claim: Makhūl reports that when the verse about a retaining ear was revealed, the Prophet asked God to make it ʿAlī’s ear; ʿAlī said he never forgot anything he heard from the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#5/r1.anchor: سمعت مكحولا يقول : لما نزل علي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وتعيها اذن واعية قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#5/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#5/r2.speaker: بريدة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#5/r2.claim: Burayda reports that the Prophet told ʿAlī God ordered him to draw ʿAlī near, teach him, and enable him to retain what he learned; the verse was revealed about this.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#5/r2.anchor: عن بريدة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلي : ' ان الله امرني ان ادنيك ولا اقصيك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p110/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p110/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p110/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reports al-Jaʿbarī’s title al-Wāʿiya, perhaps derived from 69:12, but says he found no earlier precedent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p110/r2.anchor: ولعله أخذه من وقوع قوله { وتعيها أذن واعية } ( الحاقة : 12 ) ولم أر له سلفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p110/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p110/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p110/r5.claim: The sura was called al-Ḥāqqa in the Prophet’s time and is so titled in Qurans, hadith collections, and tafsir works.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p110/r5.anchor: عنونت في المصاحف وكتب السنة وكتب التفسير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r4.claim: Recalling Noah’s people embeds gratitude for all people descended from the group saved from the flood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r4.anchor: حسن اقتضاب التذكير بأخذهم لما فيه من إدماج امتنان على جميع الناس الذين تناسلوا من الفئة الذين نجاهم الله من الغرق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r1.claim: An attentive ear is a person of understanding and an illuminated heart who hears words and receives them with comprehension and reflection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r1.anchor: عبارة عن الرجل الفهم المنور القلب، الذي يسمع القول فيتلقاه بفهم وتدبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r2.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r2.claim: Abu ʿImran al-Jawni glosses the attentive ear as one that understands from God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r2.anchor: قال أبو عمران الجوني: واعية عقلت عن الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed that the attentive ear be ʿAli’s; ʿAli says he thereafter forgot nothing he heard.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r3.anchor: ويروى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لعلي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: «إني دعوت الله تعالى أن يجعلها أذنك يا علي» . قال علي: فما سمعت بعد ذلك شيئا فنسيته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r4.claim: The majority read taʿiyaha with kasra on the ʿayn, following the pattern of talīha.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «تعيها» بكسر العين على وزن تليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير والحلواني وقنبل وابن مصرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir in the transmissions of al-Halwani and Qunbul, and Ibn Masraf, read taʿiyaha with a quiescent ʿayn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r1.anchor: «وتعيها» بسكون العين جعل التاء التي هي علامة في المضارع بمنزلة الكاف من كتف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r2.claim: The quiescent reading treats the imperfect prefix ta as inseparable from the verb, like the kaf in katif, and quiesces it for ease.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r2.anchor: جعل التاء التي هي علامة في المضارع بمنزلة الكاف من كتف إذ حرف المضارع لا يفارق الفعل فسكن تخفيفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r3.claim: A poetic line is offered for the easing, though Ibn ʿAtiyya calls it less persuasive because the verse is disconnected and allows poetic necessity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p358#2/r3.anchor: كما يقال: كتف ونحو هذا قول الشاعر: قالت سليمى اشتر لنا سويقا على أن هذا البيت منفصل، فهو أبعد لكن ضرورة الشعر تسامح به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r1.claim: “It” is the event of drowning Noah's people and saving those carried with him; it serves as a lesson and admonition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r1.anchor: لنجعلها أي لنجعل تلك الفعلة التي فعلنا من إغراق قوم نوح ونجاة من حملنا معه تذكرة أي عبرة وموعظة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r2.claim: An attentive ear preserves what it hears and acts on it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r2.anchor: وتعيها أذن واعية أي أذن تحفظ ما سمعت وتعمل به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says every ear preserves the event, so it becomes a lesson for later people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#3/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء لتحفظها كل أذن فتكون عظة لمن يأتي بعده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r1.claim: Al-jāriya is the ship moving across the water.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r1.anchor: وهي السفينة الجارية على وجه الماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r2.claim: The pronoun returns to the generic category implied by the meaning: God preserved ships of its kind for people to ride across the seas.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r2.anchor: عاد الضمير على الجنس لدلالة المعنى عليه، أي: وأبقينا لكم من جنسها ما تركبون على تيار الماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r3.claim: Qatada says God preserved Noah's Ark until the earliest generations of this community encountered it; Ibn Kathir prefers the generic reading that ships of its kind remain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: أبقى الله السفينة حتى أدركها أوائل هذه الأمة. والأول أظهر؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r4.claim: A receptive ear understands and remembers this blessing; generally, anyone with sound hearing and sound judgment can understand and heed it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the ear as retaining and hearing; Qatada says it understood from God and benefited from what it heard of the Book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حافظة سامعة (3) وقال قتادة: {أذن واعية} عقلت (4) عن الله فانتفعت بما سمعت من كتاب الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak explains that a hearing ear listened and comprehended.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {وتعيها أذن واعية} سمعتها أذن ووعت.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r7.speaker: مكحول
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r7.claim: Makhul reports that the Prophet asked God to make ʿAli a receptive ear; ʿAli said he never forgot anything he heard from the Prophet. Ibn Kathir identifies this as a mursal report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r7.anchor: سمعت مكحولا يقول: لما نزل (1) على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {وتعيها أذن واعية} قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "سألت ربي أن يجعلها أذن علي".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن بريدة الأسلمي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r8.claim: Burayda reports that the Prophet told ʿAli he was ordered to bring him close, teach him, and ensure he retained the teaching; the report says this verse was then revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p210/r8.anchor: سمعت بريدة الأسلمي يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلي: "إني أمرت أن أدنيك ولا أقصيك، وأن أعلمك وأن تعي

JISHUMI:v10p7056/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r10.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم في بعض الروايات
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r10.claim: Ibn Kathīr and some ʿĀṣim transmissions suppress the ʿayn vowel by analogy with “Show us our rites”; the author calls this reading unsatisfactory.
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r10.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم في بعض الروايات عنهما: وتعيها ساكنة العين تشبيها بقوله: ([وأرنا] مناسكنا) وهي قراءة غير مرضية

JISHUMI:v10p7056/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r11.speaker: حمزة
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r11.claim: Ḥamza gives the ʿayn a partial kasra without fully articulating it; other readers pronounce a complete kasra.
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r11.anchor: وعن حمزة بشم العين الكسرة ولا يشبعها، والقراء على كسر العين وإشباعها.

JISHUMI:v10p7056/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r13.claim: Wāʿiya receives and retains what is placed in it: the heart comprehends knowledge and possessions are kept in a container.
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r13.anchor: والواعية: القابلة لما يجعل فيها متمسكة به، وعى قلبه العلم يعي وعيا، ويقال: وعيت العلم، وأوعيت المتاع في الوعاء.

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r6.speaker: أبو بردة الأسلمي
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r6.claim: Abu Burda reports that the Prophet told Ali God ordered him to draw Ali near and teach him, and that Ali would retain it; the verse descended about this.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r6.anchor: عن أبي بردة الأسلمي أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال لعلي:

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن الحسن بن الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r7.claim: Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan reports that the Prophet prayed the verse be Ali’s ear; Ali said he never forgot anything afterward.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r7.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن الحسن بن الحسن قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: (وتعيها أذن واعية)

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r13.claim: The account of the flood and rescue is a reminder and admonition for people.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r13.anchor: لنجعلها لكم تذكرة أي: عبرة وعظة تذكرونها، يعني الخبر عنها،

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r14.claim: The account also recalls God’s favor in saving Noah’s people, punishing their unbelievers, and displaying His power and wisdom.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r14.anchor: وقيل: تذكروا بها عظم نعم الله في إنجائه وانتقامه من كفار قومه،

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r15.claim: The receptive ear retains and understands the account; alternatives say it preserves, as Ibn Abbas says, or hears and accepts.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r15.anchor: وتعيها تحفظها أذن واعية أي: تعي كل شيء، وتعلم، وقيل: حافظة، عن ابن عباس،

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r16.claim: One parses it as an imperative, wa-litaʿiyahā: let the ear hear and retain; the lām is imperative.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r16.anchor: وقيل: تقديره: ولتعيها، واللام لام الأمر، فالمراد لتسمع ولتحفظ؛

JISHUMI:v10p7060/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r1.claim: The account is a reminder meant to deter people from sin and urge obedience.
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r1.anchor: يدل قوله: (لنجعلها لكم تذكرة) أنه جعل الخبر الذي تقدم تذكرة للزجر عن المعاصي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r1.claim: The ark of Noah was made a reminder and admonition for this community; Qatada says its earliest members encountered it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r1.anchor: يعني سفينة نوح جعلها الله لكم تذكرة وعظة لهذه الأمة حتى أدركها أوائلهم في قول قتادة ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the ark's planks remained on Mount Judi.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جريج : كانت ألواحها على الجودي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r3.claim: One gloss of a receptive ear is an ear that hears.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the ear is believing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r5.claim: A second gloss from Ibn Abbas is an ear that retains what it hears.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r5.anchor: الثالث : حافظة , وهذا قول ابن عباس أيضا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj distinguishes wa'aytu, retaining something within oneself, from aw'aytu, retaining it for someone else.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج : يقال وعيت لما حفظته في نفسك , وأوعيت لما حفظته في غيرك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r7.claim: Qatada says it is an ear that understands God and benefits from what it hears of the Quran.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r7.anchor: أذن عقلت عن الله وانتفعت بما سمعت من كتاب الله , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r8.claim: Makḥul reports that when the verse descended, the Prophet asked God to make Ali its receptive ear; Makḥul adds that Ali said he never forgot anything he heard from the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80/r8.anchor: وروى مكحول أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال عند نزول هذه الآية :

MUQATIL:69:5-12/r17.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r17.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r17.claim: The destruction of Noah’s people was made a lesson and admonition for their descendants and later generations.
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r17.anchor: { لنجعلها لكم } يعني لكي نجعلها لكم، يعني في هلاك قوم نوح لكم يا معشر الأبناء { تذكرة } يعني عظة وتذكرة

MUQATIL:69:5-12/r18.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r18.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r18.claim: An attentive ear retains what it hears and benefits from the admonition.
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r18.anchor: يعني حافظة لما سعمت فانتفعت بما سمعت من الموعظة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r1.claim: “It” refers to the event of saving the believers and drowning the unbelievers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r1.anchor: أي الفعلة وهي انجاء المؤمنين وإغراق الكافرين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r2.claim: The event is a lesson and admonition for you.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r3.claim: The reading with ḍamma on the dhāl is used by all except Nāfiʿ.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r3.anchor: بضم الذال غير نافع ﴿ واعية ﴾ حافظة لما تسمع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r4.claim: A retentive ear preserves what it hears.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r5.speaker: قتادة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r5.claim: Qatadah says it is an ear that understands from God and benefits from what it hears.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#8/r5.anchor: قال قتادة وهي اذن عقلت عن الله وانتفعت بما سمعت

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.claim: The stories of destroyed peoples warn this community against disobeying the Messenger; God favors them as descendants of the rescued, carried in their ancestors' loins.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.anchor: والمقصود من قصص هذه الأمم وذكر ما حل بهم من العذاب: زجر هذه الأمة عن الاقتداء بهم في معصية الرسول. ثم من عليهم بأن جعلهم ذرية من نجا من الغرق

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r8.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to Noah's ship, which God made a reminder and admonition for this community.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r8.anchor: { لنجعلها لكم تذكرة } يعني سفينة نوح عليه الصلاة والسلام. جعلها الله تذكرة وعظة لهذه الأمة

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r9.claim: Qatada says the early generations encountered the surviving ship.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r9.anchor: حتى أدركها أوائلهم في قول قتادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the ship's planks remained on Mount Judi; the preserved timbers reminded people of Noah's people and their ancestors' rescue, unlike other ships that became dust.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r10.anchor: قال ابن جريج: كانت ألواحها على الجودي. والمعنى: أبقيت لكم تلك الخشبات حتى تذكروا ما حل بقوم نوح

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r11.claim: Another view makes the drowning of Noah's people and rescue of believers the reminder, rather than the vessel itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r11.anchor: وقيل: لنجعل تلك الفعلة من إغراق قوم نوح وإنجاء من آمن معه موعظة لكم

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r12.claim: An aware ear preserves and hears the reminder, retaining what comes from God; the ship itself cannot be described as an aware ear.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r12.anchor: أي تحفظها وتسمعها أذن حافظة لما جاء من عند الله. والسفينة لا توصف بهذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r13.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj distinguishes waʿaytu, retaining something in oneself, from awʿaytu, preserving something in a container outside oneself.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r13.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويقال وعيت كذا أي حفظته في نفسي، أعيه وعيا. ووعيت العلم، ووعيت ما قلت كله بمعنى.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r14.speaker: طلحة، حميد، الأعرج
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r14.claim: Talha, Humayd, and al-Aʿraj read wa-taʿiyahā with a still ʿayn, likening it to arinā; reports differ for Asim and Ibn Kathir, while the rest read with kasra.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r15.claim: Qurtubi links the attentive ear to the reminder for one who has a heart in 50:37.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r15.anchor: إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r1.claim: Qatada says the aware ear understands what comes from God and benefits from hearing His Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r1.anchor: وقال قتادة: الأذن الواعية أذن عقلت عن الله تعالى، وانتفعت بما سمعت من كتاب الله عز وجل.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r2.claim: Makhul reports that at the verse's revelation the Prophet asked God to make Ali the receptive ear; Ali said he never forgot anything he heard from the Prophet. Al-Mawardi cites it.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r2.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال عند نزول هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan's similar report, cited by al-Thaʿlabi, has the Prophet ask that Ali's ear be receptive; Ali swears he forgot nothing thereafter.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r3.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:«سألت ربي أن يجعلها أذنك يا علي»

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r4.claim: Abu Barza al-Aslami reports the Prophet telling Ali that God ordered him to make Ali hear, include and teach him, with God's guarantee that he would retain the teaching.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12#2/r4.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلي
